body:
**Stable key:** `MEM-P06`  
**Difficulty:** **High**  
**Suggested label:** `difficulty:high` (metadata proposal; a title/body marker does not depend on label availability)  
**Planning baseline:** `Ozwasyd/FsusBlog@580cf1af614fd0edab9cb4c9ee95ec4e128b0327`  
**Acceptance predecessors:** `MEM-P01` (#3445), `MEM-P05` (#3451), `MEM-AUTO` (#3454)

### Objective

Change PublicHotRead payload storage while retaining the existing wire, security, routing, content identity, and transport behavior.

### Source and scope precedence

This issue implements stage P06 of the user-supplied memory-governance report (version 1.0, 2026-09-15). The user's later requirement for default automatic discovery and activation supersedes `Preferred`, default-off, and mandatory manual-per-capability opt-in wording. Original work-item IDs are preserved for traceability. Baseline paths must be checked against the actual implementation candidate; this issue is not a claim that proposed types already exist.

### Mandatory policy and terminology

All configurable capabilities default to `Auto` when omitted. `Auto` means automatic discovery, bounded qualification, online activation, and deterministic selection for an eligible workload after resource admission. It does not mean indiscriminate allocation. A supported, release-qualified and runtime-qualified available path must not require a second enable flag, per-host approval file, or administrator confirmation. `Disabled` prevents new capability-specific probes and use, and drains existing owners before disposal. `Required` adds a strict requirement; it does not override safety, permissions, qualification, or budgets. The earlier report value `Preferred` is superseded, not an additional mode.

Detection, qualification, online state, effective path, and per-operation admission are separate facts. Unknown, Unsupported, NotVerified, Faulted, Disabled, and temporarily BudgetRejected are not synonyms. A missing signal is not zero usage. Qualifying a release/backend is not a manual opt-in on each deployment. The always-required accounting, ownership, and content-security rules are not optional capability switches.

### Scope and exclusions

No new L0 disk/GPU miss path, HTTP stack replacement, protocol extension, in-place nonce mutation, or production dual-cache construction is included.

All product implementation introduced by this memory program remains C#/.NET. Supported already-installed OS/GPU APIs may be called through isolated C# adapters. Existing unrelated C++, frontend, protocol, and business components are not rewritten. Do not change AEDS/HTTP, authorization, revocation, publication, or delivery authority merely to simplify memory management.

### Files and ownership

| Status | Path or owner | Required treatment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| B | `src/backend/Infrastructure/PublicReadArtifacts/PublicHotReadFastPath.cs` | Artifact, snapshot, store, and native backing attachment. |
| B | `src/backend/Infrastructure/PublicReadArtifacts/PublicHotReadFastPath.Serving.cs` | Lease-scoped writes and completion handling. |
| B | `src/backend/Infrastructure/PublicReadArtifacts/PublicHotReadFastPath.Routing.cs` | Preserve route and result-class semantics. |
| B | `src/backend/Infrastructure/PublicReadArtifacts/PublicHotReadResidency.cs` | Backing-aware logical statistics and ledger projection. |
| R | `Existing artifact-integrity and CSP nonce-template owners` | Locate exact files and retain their qualification authority. |
| N | `src/backend/Infrastructure/Memory/Host/` | CPU lease adapters only; no disk or device masquerading as Memory. |

B = baseline-reported; N = proposed-new; R = exact owner unresolved until MEM-P00. Paths and namespaces in this table are scope locators, not permission to create a parallel registry, publisher, scheduler, configuration source, or test runner. New tests must reside inside the actual owning project.

### Required implementation work

- [ ] **P06.1** Preserve the useful ReadOnlyMemory surfaces of binary and HTML artifacts while introducing explicit snapshot and read leases. Use native MemoryManager backing rather than forcing an unrelated public handle API through the repository.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P06-AC01`, `MEM-P06-AC02`.
- [ ] **P06.2** Audit every array assumption in serving, integrity, serialization, and compression consumers. Any unavoidable array-only adapter must have an explicit bounded reservation and a measured copy; native mode must not silently materialize another full-sized managed array.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P06-AC04`.
- [ ] **P06.3** Acquire the qualified read lease within the existing route/security flow and keep it until the actual consumer has stopped using the source. Preserve original Task/ValueTask, cancellation, abort, and backpressure semantics. Do not claim end-to-end zero copy.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P06-AC03`, `MEM-P06-AC05`.
- [ ] **P06.4** Keep immutable HTML shared and read-only. Build per-request nonce mutations in separately budgeted scratch owned through actual send completion. Preserve original template integrity, multilingual handling, and representation qualification.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P06-AC02`, `MEM-P06-AC06`.
- [ ] **P06.5** Make residency statistics backing-aware. Preserve historical logical metric meanings, distinguish managed-array/LOH observations from native capacity, and obtain globally deduplicated allocation charges from the ledger.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P06-AC07`.
- [ ] **P06.6** Run managed/native byte-level differential fixtures for raw and compressed frames, HTML, headers, statuses, sensitive bypass, revocation, and version stickiness. Dual construction is test-only, not a default production memory multiplier.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P06-AC02`, `MEM-P06-AC08`, `MEM-P06-AC09`, `MEM-P06-AC10`.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **MEM-P06-AC01** With omitted settings and a qualified native host backend, MEM-AUTO selects native backing for the registered eligible workload without a separate enable flag. Explicit Disabled selects the valid baseline and causes no new native allocation.
- [ ] **MEM-P06-AC02** For each canonical fixture, managed/native outputs have identical stable bytes, status, and required headers. Request-specific nonce differences meet the original nonce and CSP validator rather than being ignored.
- [ ] **MEM-P06-AC03** T10/T11 demonstrate that retire, abort, cancellation, and backpressure never release source or scratch before actual consumption ends. ValueTask completion is not consumed twice.
- [ ] **MEM-P06-AC04** A native artifact with no backing array serves successfully without an unbudgeted fallback ToArray. The copy counter and capacity trace account for every deliberate compatibility copy.
- [ ] **MEM-P06-AC05** An L0 hit performs no disk I/O, GPU transfer, capability probe, driver initialization, pressure-file read, database query, or Redis query. The test uses forbidden-operation hooks, not only throughput inference.
- [ ] **MEM-P06-AC06** Nonce processing cannot mutate the shared template or another response. Non-ASCII and length-changing fixtures remain valid and qualification digests preserve their established meaning.
- [ ] **MEM-P06-AC07** Native slices do not increment managed-array or LOH-array counts. Shared block capacity is charged once even when several artifact variants or generations refer to it.
- [ ] **MEM-P06-AC08** Not-resident and authoritative not-found remain distinguishable; authentication-sensitive routes retain their bypass; revoked content cannot be served by last-good or by changing storage mode.
- [ ] **MEM-P06-AC09** Latency, CPU, peak capacity, and build behavior pass the frozen P01 gates under comparable delivered-result mix. Missing performance evidence does not become a claim of native speedup.
- [ ] **MEM-P06-AC10** Safe disable prevents new native acquisitions/allocations as specified, drains already borrowed data, and selects a qualified fallback for new work without a whole-cache copy.

### Required validation scope

Current-stage contract and actual integration tests for the implementation in this issue. Real platform/device evidence is mandatory for every support row this issue claims.

| Scenario | Responsibility in this issue | Required observable assertion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `T10`: Transport write remains incomplete while the snapshot retires | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P04 | No release before actual consumer completion; eventual release after all remaining holds end. |
| `T11`: Outer wait cancels while underlying work continues | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P04 | Cancellation does not return source, staging, context, or operation reservations before actual completion. |
| `T13`: Repeated disposal, ownership misuse, and outstanding pins | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P04 | Release is idempotent or rejected explicitly; no underflow, double free, or stale-token/ABA reuse. |
| `T18`: Equivalent managed, native, and flat-index fixtures | Primary implementation owner | Stable bytes, required headers, statuses, and content eligibility are equivalent; volatile fields use explicit validators. |
| `T19`: Encoding variants, HEAD, 304, nonce HTML, and locales | Primary implementation owner | Preserve variant identity, CSP/nonce isolation, and existing external serving semantics. |
| `T20`: Revocation or visibility change races with location publication | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P12 | Do not republish an obsolete qualified representation; inspect the location index as well as the response. |
| `T52`: Disable or rollback while readers/operations remain | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P20 | Stop new work, drain old holds, and avoid forced Free or whole-cache/device readback. |
| `T53`: Continuous pressure events and diagnostics | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P20 | Bound buffers, log volume, and label cardinality and prevent private-data disclosure. |

### Evidence and acceptance rules

Every unchecked acceptance criterion below is mandatory. `must` and `must not` are normative; `may` grants an option only where it is explicitly stated. A required test passes only when its specified assertion is observed on the current candidate. A comment stating that an assertion is true is not evidence.

Bind evidence to the actual commit and worktree fingerprint, fixture, toolchain, configuration revision, backend, OS/architecture, relevant driver/device identity, actual command, and raw result. Use the existing test DAG, required static admission, fixture ownership, and independent verifiers. All numeric limits and performance expressions referenced by this issue must be finite, explicit, and frozen by their owning policy/baseline before candidate results are examined. Missing values block acceptance; do not invent a passing threshold afterward.

Expected resource rejection must not conceal use-after-free, bounds violations, double free, uninitialized disclosure, revoked/wrong content, negative accounting, a parallel authority, or an unbounded queue. Any such correctness failure blocks acceptance regardless of performance. Do not rewrite frozen receipts or weaken tests. Missing platform or hardware evidence is `NotVerified`, not `Passed` or a convenient `NotApplicable`.

Evidence level is stage-specific: contract or fixture work may run before a downstream backend exists, but it does not certify that backend. Each primary implementation owner must supply its own required integration/platform evidence; MEM-P19 independently closes the complete matrix. Passing tests never authorizes automatic closure of this issue, another issue, or a pull request.

### Safe disable and rollback

Select the previous qualified backing for new generations and safely drain native data. Do not undo content revocation or remove global reservation enforcement.

### Completion report

Report the exact scope and files changed, every acceptance-criterion result, tests and commands actually run, raw current-source evidence, default Auto behavior, negative/competition cases, performance against frozen gates where applicable, unresolved support rows, and rollback results. A missing required environment leaves the corresponding promise unverified. Do not describe planned tests or a passing document validator as product verification.

Docker-related tests are not to be executed by this delivery agent under the project restriction. State them explicitly as not run. A Docker-specific assertion requires evidence from its authorized owner; a genuinely technology-independent assertion may use authorized non-Docker isolation. Do not fetch missing implementation dependencies from the network; record exact package/version/target gaps and stop the blocked execution item.
